answer.rationale: The vendor is outside servicing personnel, but coordination under §1910.147(f)(2)(i) applies only when those personnel will engage in activities covered by the lockout/tagout standard. Coverage depends on whether the maintenance involves a machine or equipment for which unexpected energizing, startup, or release of stored energy could occur and cause injury. If that predicate is met, the on-site and outside employers must inform each other of their respective lockout/tagout procedures, and applicable energy-control procedures must be developed, documented, and used.
answer.missing_information_or_escalation_reason: Determine whether the planned routine maintenance exposes workers to potentially hazardous unexpected energization, startup, or stored/residual-energy release that could cause injury. The supplied facts do not establish that coverage predicate.
